verdict.rationale: Name.com's own docs show a WHOIS privacy capability: an API endpoint that enables privacy protection on a domain, and privacy listed among manageable domain settings. Nothing in the evidence shows it is free or on by default, and an explicit 'enable' endpoint suggests it may be opt-in. Missing for 10: evidence that privacy is free with no upsell, evidence that it is on by default at registration, documentation of which fields (name, address, email) are redacted, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, WHOIS privacy is free and on by default — my name, address, and email stay redacted without an upsell

citations.quote: Enables WHOIS privacy protection on a domain.
manage domain settings (locks, privacy, autorenew, contacts)
